quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The stressed second syllable is short, open and lightly rounded.
quests.explanation: The short rounded vowel is in the stressed second syllable. The final syllables are weak, and the ph is /f/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Keep one short, steady, slightly rounded shape for /ɒ/. Any closing of the lips would turn it into /əʊ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Despite how the word looks, the vowel closes.
quests.explanation: The ph is /f/, and the first syllable closes in a glide. A short vowel would give 'troffy'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Only /əʊ/ has a start and an end point; /ɒ/ is a single position.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The g is silent and the stressed syllable glides.
quests.explanation: The first vowel is wide and the stressed second syllable glides. Only the glide is being asked.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Many learners shorten /eɪ/ to /e/. Extend it and feel the jaw close.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The sci spells /ʃ/. The first syllable is short and rounded.
quests.explanation: The sci spells /ʃ/, and no vowel follows it. The first syllable is short and rounded.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Lip rounding is the clearest cue: /ɒ/ has it, /ʌ/ does not.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE SECOND SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The first part closes in a glide; the target is later.
quests.explanation: The first syllable has a closing diphthong that isn't part of this pair. The second syllable ends in the glide to schwa.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The glide to schwa is the signature of /eə/. Listen for the tail, not for the start.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Ear spelling again, with no lip rounding.
quests.explanation: Ear spells the steady vowel in 'earn', 'earth' and 'learn'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Check your lips: still and unrounded for /ɜː/, a clear oval for /ɔː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: A wide jaw in the first syllable; the rest is weak.
quests.explanation: The wide vowel is in the stressed first syllable. The u in the second part belongs to /bjʊ/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: For /æ/ the tongue body pushes forward against the lower teeth. For /ʌ/ it relaxes in the middle with no forward push.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The ai spelling in the first syllable glides.
quests.explanation: The ai spelling in the first syllable glides. The e in the spelling sits in weak syllables.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The spellings a_e, ai, ay and eigh give /eɪ/; a single e before a consonant (bed, pen) gives /e/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Five letters, two sounds: a /j/ glide and a long rounded vowel.
quests.explanation: Five letters make two sounds: a /j/ glide and the long rounded vowel. Everything after the first u is silent spelling.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The quality gap is larger than the length gap. /ʊ/ is not simply a shortened /uː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FINAL SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The last syllable is short and rounded, while the first has a glide.
quests.explanation: The ue is silent, and the short rounded vowel is in the final syllable. The initial diphthong is a different sound.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /əʊ/ glides from central to a rounded back position; /ɒ/ is a short, steady, open rounded vowel.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: After the first-syllable diphthong, the second syllable needs a wide jaw.
quests.explanation: The wide vowel is in the stressed second syllable. The first syllable has a diphthong, so don't confuse the two.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spread the lips slightly for both, but let the jaw do the work: /e/ stops about halfway, /æ/ keeps going.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Spelling and sound have nothing in common here. Lips neutral.
quests.explanation: It sounds exactly like 'kernel', with the steady central vowel. The spelling is famously unrelated to the sound.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Here spelling is no help at all: /ɜː/ with flat lips, not the rounded /ɔː/ that the o might suggest.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: It has three syllables in speech, not four: 'vej-ta-bl'. The stressed first syllable is half open.
quests.explanation: The stressed first syllable has the short half-open vowel. The spelling suggests an extra vowel in the middle, but speakers drop it, so count syllables by ear.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If a word with /æ/ is coming out as /e/, check that the front of the tongue is low, not hovering at mid-height.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Silent ch and a short, rounded vowel.
quests.explanation: A short rounded vowel. The ch is silent, and the spelling is famously opaque.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɔː/ is longer, higher and more strongly rounded; /ɒ/ is short, more open and only lightly rounded.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The first part glides; the second part is short and open.
quests.explanation: The first syllable has the glide, and the final syllable has a short vowel that isn't part of this pair.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /eɪ/ glides from mid-front up toward /ɪ/; /e/ is a short, steady half-open vowel.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The p is silent; the stress is on the second syllable.
quests.explanation: The p is silent, and the stressed second syllable has the short rounded vowel. The initial diphthong isn't part of this pair.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short and fairly open, so duration gives no help. Listen for the darker, back quality of /ɒ/ against the brighter, more central /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The ear spelling again: a steady vowel in the stressed syllable.
quests.explanation: Er in the stressed second syllable spells the steady vowel, so don't glide it as you would in 'bear'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Hold /ɜː/ perfectly still: ear spells both /ɜː/ (rehearse) and /eə/ (bear), and only the absence of a glide gives it away.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE THIRD SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The target is the long open vowel in the third syllable.
quests.explanation: The arch spelling gives a long open vowel in the third syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are open and back, so the lips are the main difference: neutral for /ɑː/, slightly rounded for /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FINAL SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The final syllable carries the main stress and ends in a glide.
quests.explanation: The final syllable carries the main stress and the glide. The first syllable has a long rounded vowel with secondary stress.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪə/ starts at /ɪ/ and glides to schwa; /iː/ is a pure, steady, tense vowel.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE THIRD SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The third syllable carries the main stress: short and rounded.
quests.explanation: The stressed third syllable has the short rounded vowel. The first syllable has a long open vowel with secondary stress.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Think of the lips first: a small rounded gap for /ɒ/, a loose unrounded one for /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: After the first syllable, the second is long and open.
quests.explanation: The ts is /ts/ and the first vowel is long and rounded. The long open vowel is in the stressed second syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue is pushed forward for /æ/ and pulled back and down for /ɑː/. Feel the tongue root move.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The stressed second syllable ends in a glide.
quests.explanation: The first syllable has the short rounded vowel, and the stressed second syllable ends in a glide.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Say /e/ with no movement. For /eɪ/ let the jaw rise and the tongue slide upward towards the end.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The oo spelling is a trap: the vowel closes.
quests.explanation: It rhymes with 'coach', not with 'booth'. The oo spelling is a trap, and the vowel closes.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The lips close up through /əʊ/ and finish in a small round. For /ɒ/ the jaw stays open and the lips stable.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The first syllable carries secondary stress: lips neutral.
quests.explanation: Wor- gives the steady central vowel, so the lips stay flat in the first syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɜː/ is central with neutral or slightly spread lips; /ɔː/ is back with clearly rounded lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE SECOND SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The target is the nun syllable, which has secondary stress. Think of the verb 'pronounce', then change the vowel.
quests.explanation: The second syllable has the central vowel, spelled u. The verb 'pronounce' has a different vowel, spelled ou.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ sits further back and a little lower; /ʌ/ is more central. The tongue moves forward and slightly up from /ɒ/ to /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Drop the jaw in the second syllable, where the word's stress sits.
quests.explanation: The wide vowel is in the stressed second syllable. The final glide isn't part of this pair.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Before nasals and voiced stops /æ/ tends to lengthen while /e/ stays brief, but the jaw gap is still the deciding cue.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: After /kj/, the stressed second syllable is long and rounded.
quests.explanation: The stressed second syllable has the long vowel, spelled u.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a mirror, /uː/ shows a tight forward pout and /ʊ/ a gentle, relaxed circle.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Both vowels in this word belong to the pair. Take the first.
quests.explanation: The first syllable stays flat and central, while the last syllable rounds. This one word lets you hear and feel both in a single breath.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɜː/ stays flat and central, while /ɔː/ rounds. This one word contains both, so you can hear and feel the difference in a single breath.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The word that names what you've been practising. A wide start, then the lips round.
quests.explanation: It begins wide open, glides to a rounded vowel and finishes with schwa. A relaxed start would sound like 'vole'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Open the jaw wide first for /aʊ/. If you start relaxed, you will produce /əʊ/ instead.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The a is long and open: this word belongs to the BATH set, like 'master'.
quests.explanation: 'Master' and 'mastery' follow the BATH pattern in RP, so the wide front vowel would be wrong here.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Final check on a pattern you met early: BATH words take long open /ɑː/ in RP, however much the spelling looks like TRAP.
